description: The line plot illustrates the loss ratio (%) as a function of TFLOPs (trillion floating-point operations) for different models, including a baseline "Vanilla" model and several variants of SepLLM. The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs," is presented on a logarithmic scale, ranging from $1 \times 10^7$ to $9 \times 10^8$, with tick marks at powers of ten. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio (%)," is linear and ranges from 94% to 99%, with major gridlines at 1% intervals. The legend identifies five distinct lines: "Vanilla" (purple, triangle markers, solid line), "SepLLM (n=64)" (orange, square markers, solid line), "SepLLM (n=128)" (blue, cross markers, solid line), "SepLLM (n=64, H)" (green, diamond markers, solid line), and "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" (red, circle markers, solid line). The "Vanilla" model maintains a high loss ratio, starting at approximately 97.1% and remaining relatively stable around 99.5% across all TFLOPs. The "SepLLM (n=64)" model starts at a lower loss ratio of about 98.1% and increases to a peak of approximately 99.7% at $4 \times 10^8$ TFLOPs before slightly declining. The "SepLLM (n=128)" model begins at a loss ratio of about 97.1% and steadily increases to a peak of approximately 99.5% at $2 \times 10^8$ TFLOPs, after which it remains relatively flat. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" model starts at a loss ratio of about 97.5% and increases to a peak of approximately 99.7% at $5 \times 10^8$ TFLOPs, then slightly declines. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" model shows a dramatic increase in loss ratio, starting at 94% and rising sharply to a peak of approximately 98.9% at $2 \times 10^8$ TFLOPs, after which it fluctuates slightly but remains below 99%.
